items.summary: Axios reports that OpenAI is preparing a public-relations campaign after the midterm elections, when Democrats may regain control of Congress. The company's chief global affairs officer Chris Lehane told Axios about several proposals, including rebranding data centers as 'AI compute campuses.' He described the surrounding debate as healthy and said communities should hold companies accountable for transformative benefits.
items.title: OpenAI Plans Rebranding Data Centers as AI Compute Campuses

items.summary: Business correspondent Timothy Goh, via an AI-generated askST Jobs column, asks how employees should respond when a boss uses sarcasm or indirect remarks. Michelle Koh of The Edge Partnership says staff should answer the manager’s words with calm questions rather than react to tone; David Leong of PeopleWorldwide Consulting adds that making implicit displeasure explicit disarms passive aggression while preserving respect and professionalism.
items.title: Singapore experts advise on handling passive-aggressive bosses

items.summary: Ben Goodman, Adobe’s Asia-Pacific and Japan president, argues in an interview with The Straits Times that AI raises the bar for content rather than destroying art. He says audiences are becoming more discerning, which increases demand for quality and enables personalisation beyond demographics. Adobe reported subscription revenue of US$4.7 billion (S$6 billion) from creative and marketing professionals for its fiscal third quarter ended Aug 28, up 13% year on year. Goodman said the company is not deterred by a roughly 25% share decline this year, citing AI adoption as a growth driver. He highlighted Singapore’s strong enterprise ecosystem as an important strategic hub.
items.title: Adobe APAC Chief Frames AI as a Quality Catalyst

items.summary: On October 6, the Privacy Center at Georgetown Law School hosted Life After Data: The Conference on De-datafication, prompting a discussion of whether to abandon or rebuild today's internet. Panelists offered varied views. Douglas Rushkoff urged leaving it entirely; Anika Collier Navaroli said egos must be killed and that the next generation should lead. Bridget Todd wants to keep what is worth saving while discarding tracking and manipulation, noting AI makes the bargain worse. Konstantinos Komaitis argued people need not leave but should resist platform concentration and protect agency. Caddie Alford reported her Virginia Commonwealth University class of about 22 students see a mass exodus as unlikely and name billionaires and politicians as obstacles. Janet Vertesi said an alternative internet already exists, citing the Veilid organization and open-source tools shaped by Europe's AI Act and data privacy regulations. Alice Marwick called for dismantling the business of buying and selling data. Liz Orembo stressed openness must survive alongside new data and AI infrastructure. Robin Berjon pointed to ATProto as a promising architectural change. B Cavello emphasized attention and agency over revealed preferences.
items.title: Voices on Abandoning and Rebuilding the Internet

items.summary: Dazzle AI CEO Marissa Mayer, OpenAI's Sam Altman and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg have drawn criticism for comments praising AI in everyday life. The remarks prompted TechCrunch's Amanda Silberling to question whether such executives are too disconnected from ordinary users — a concern amplified as Anthropic prepares an IPO amid waning Wall Street appetite for heavy AI spending. On the Equity podcast, hosts Kirsten Korosec and Sean O'Kane discussed the issue with Silberling. She suggested the problem is partly marketing and partly product, noting that industry leaders are pushing a future where basic human interaction gets optimized out of occurring, adding that humans talking to each other may be net positive for society.
items.title: Tech CEOs' AI remarks spark out-of-touch debate

items.summary: The FBI confirmed that North Korean state-sponsored hackers known as TraderTraitor were responsible for the $6.3 billion crypto-theft attack on Binance, calling it the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. In a Saturday security alert, the agency attributed the breach to TraderTraitor, also tracked as Lazarus Group, Jade Sleet, and APT38. The FBI quoted North Korea stealing more than $6 billion in virtual assets from Binance around October 29, 2026. Blockchain firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis had earlier linked the theft to TraderTraitor. Binance said it plans to resume withdrawals on November 1 between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC and has covered about 95% of impacted funds, pledging not to pass losses onto users.
items.title: FBI Attributes Record Binance Crypto Heist to North Korean Hackers

items.summary: Eli Electric Vehicles teased a new version of its tiny electric microcar, the Eli ZERO MX, ahead of EICMA in Milan. The company described it as an L7e vehicle joining its lineup and also hinted at a Race Edition with sportier styling. Unlike the familiar European model capped at 45 km/h (28 mph), L7e vehicles can typically reach up to 80-90 km/h, which could make the EV more practical for longer trips while keeping its small footprint.
items.title: Eli previews faster electric microcar at Milan show

items.summary: Despite Google's promise of a carbon-free future by 2030, its new Project Skyway data centre in Pine Island, Minnesota, faces strong opposition. The proposal pairs the facility with Xcel Energy to add wind, solar and battery storage capacity. A lawsuit from the Minnesota Centre for Environmental Advocacy challenges vague environmental reviews, while local surveys show roughly three-quarters of participants oppose construction. Google's agreement includes minimum demand charges and exit fees to protect grid investment against falling AI demand. The plan remains pending approval from the Minnesota Public Utilities Commission amid broader concerns over consumer protections and water use.
items.title: Google's Minnesota Data Centre Draws Local and Environmental Backlash

items.summary: The article revisits how Trump’s One Big, Beautiful Bill Act strengthened the IRS Section 179 deduction for 2025. Because the IRS does not separate electric from diesel trucks by fuel type, both qualify under depreciation rules; tractor units are classified as 3-year properties eligible for 100% bonus depreciation acquired after January 19, 2025. The Section 179 expense limit doubled to $2.5 million, with a phase-out beginning at $4 million and ending at $6.5 million of capital investments. Businesses may combine Section 179 expensing with bonus depreciation under revised Section 168(k), potentially deducting the full cost of qualifying electric equipment in the first year. The author notes tax law is complex and advises consulting a certified accountant before acting.
items.title: Expanded Section 179 Deduction May Boost Commercial EV Fleet Purchases

items.summary:
Residents of Taylor, Texas, a rural town of roughly 17,000 people about 35 miles northeast of Austin, are opposing a wave of data center construction. Samsung broke ground in 2022 on a $17 billion semiconductor facility on a 1,200-acre campus near their homes. Since then the city approved three more projects: Blueprint Projects, KDC Project Comal and Taylor Technology Campus (formerly Project Mustang). By some estimates the three would consume 1.42 gigawatts of electricity, enough to power about 950,000 Texas homes a year or roughly Austin’s annual footprint. The HALT Taylor coalition gathered 1,400 signatures over 130 days for a ballot measure seeking a moratorium; the city denied it on June 25 and instead plans code amendments effective by 2027 that would not cover already-approved facilities. Residents also filed a land-misuse lawsuit against Blueprint Projects, which Judge Ryan D. Larson dismissed in October 2025 but is under appeal. Attorney General Ken Paxton announced an investigation on Sept. 17 into whether the original parkland deed clause restricts development.

items.summary: Startup Energy North scrapped its June 28, 2028 start date for Project Ares, one of Australia's largest planned data centres, after the Northern Territory environment regulator suspended its seven-week deadline and sought federal advice. The move marks the biggest timing reversal among Australian projects amid a global push to build AI infrastructure by 2030. Energy North said it would confirm dates once environmental terms are set; Daniel Hunter called the old date merely indicative. The project, on land 683 km from Darwin, faces scrutiny over water use and Aboriginal sites, with regulators citing low confidence in mitigation measures.
items.title: Energy North Scraps Data Centre Timeline After Regulator Stalls

items.summary: An analysis published Friday by KFF, the health research group, projects that the average price of health insurance in the Obamacare marketplaces will rise 13 percent next year. The forecast draws on new prices for 2027 released by the Trump administration across 30 states with federally managed markets and additional state figures. KFF estimates the cheapest bronze plan with a high deductible could cost about $700 monthly for a 50-year-old single person, citing Ms. Cox of the group as its source.
items.title: KFF Forecasts Health Insurance Price Rise on New Trump Administration Data

items.summary: An article argues that former chancellor Rachel Reeves has shaped Andy Burnham's government agenda, though it notes she received no credit for her role. Reeves is set to speak at Harvard about Brexit damage and the case for closer EU ties, arguing Europe represents both a credible and radical choice. Her call to share national taxes with regional leaders now forms the centrepiece of chancellor John Healey's budget. The article states fiscal rules were changed to allow up to £100bn in new capital spending, which is flowing into NHS infrastructure, roads, housing, rail upgrades and energy investments. It observes that Burnham may begin seeing investment benefits if he avoids an early election.
items.title: Reeves's economic blueprint shapes Burnham government agenda

items.summary: Business Today published a daily financial horoscope dated November 2, 2026, offering predictions to readers of several zodiac signs. The piece leads with the Libra sign, stating that its individuals will benefit from professional relationships and that their financial matters will be in their favour. It then turns through Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, Virgo, Scorpio, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius and Pisces, each receiving a short forecast on profit, savings or caution around transactions. The article carries no figures beyond the date itself; it is framed as opinion rather than fact. A disclaimer notes that astrological predictions are the opinions of an astrologer based on planetary positions, and that Business Today accepts no responsibility for them.
items.title: Financial Horoscope for Libra and Other Signs on November 2, 2026

items.summary: A Hindi news roundup previews five top stories, opening with a Ministry of Finance report projecting India's GDP growth at 7.35%, alongside inflation and foreign-exchange-reserve estimates. It also covers Prime Minister Modi's Gujarat visit promising ₹19,000 crore to farmers, Delhi market concerns ahead of Congress rallies on November 1, IndiGo signaling higher fares after a September loss, and a dispute over IDBI Bank's ₹53,000 crore sale between Rahul Gandhi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.
items.title: India GDP Growth Forecast at 7.35% as Five Major Stories Surface

items.summary: London’s mayor Sadiq Khan has called for a cap on the numbers of robotaxis operating on its streets, with the UK government poised to allow fully driverless vehicles in the capital. He said politicians had failed to grasp the pace of change from the technology, which could threaten jobs and increase congestion. His comments followed Chinese robotaxis being tested in London by Freenow by Lyft, a rival to Uber, and limited services offered by Wayve’s self-driving cars under licence from Transport for London (TfL). Khan said there was no cap on private hire vehicles or taxis at the moment and that London needed more regulatory powers. He warned against ‘a big bang without proper regulation in place’ before any mass rollout.
items.title: Khan calls for cap on robotaxis in London

items.summary: A rare humanitarian ceasefire allowing civilians to evacuate the occupied city of Oleshky has ended after being due to finish at 22:59 Ukrainian time. Fighting continued elsewhere, and overnight Russia struck energy infrastructure in four regions, leaving hundreds of thousands without power; one strike killed two people including a 13-year-old girl in Vinnytsia. Ukraine hit a missile fuel producer near Rostov. President Zelensky called the strikes 'extremely high' over the past week and urged more Patriot missiles.
items.title: Ceasefire in Kherson ends as Russian strikes cut power across Ukraine

items.summary: A Learjet 60 carrying nine people crashed into a residential area in Palm Beach County, Florida on Sunday, exploding into a large fireball near passing vehicles. Federal officials said the Bahamas-bound jet had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas. It remains unclear whether anyone onboard survived or if ground casualties occurred.
items.title: Business Jet Crashes in Florida, Killing Nine People

items.summary: Sofia Demetriades, an 18-year-old violinist from Leicestershire studying at the Royal Academy of Music, won the BBC Young Musician competition 2026. Judges Joanna MacGregor, Ben Gernon and Errollyn Wallen praised her performance of Tchaikovsky’s Violin Concerto as full of insights, poetry and maturity. The biennial contest, created in 1978 by Humphrey Burton, reached its first all-female final.
items.title: Teenage violinist wins BBC Young Musician 2026 in first all-female final

items.summary: In his October budget speech, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced that spouses of expatriates holding a Category 1 employment pass will be allowed to work in Malaysia from Jan 1, 2027. Recruiters and relocation experts say the change addresses trailing-spouse unemployment among dual-career families who otherwise leave within months. Eligible expats must earn at least RM20,000 (US$4,900) a month for the pass. The Malaysia HR Forum and Malaysian Employers' Federation welcomed it as an appeal boost while urging clearer implementation terms. Some economists called it only a minor adjustment amid broader visa concerns.
items.title: Malaysia Eases Work Rules for Expat Spouses

items.summary: NUS landscape architecture professor Yun Hye Hwang argues that framing the Housing and Development Board's revised Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks plans as winners versus losers reinforces zero-sum thinking. The Housing and Development Board announced on Wednesday (Oct 28) a cut of about 1,200 homes across both sites while retaining an additional six hectares of greenery. HDB received approximately 9,500 public submissions and engaged around 1,000 stakeholders following the July announcement. In a joint statement issued on Oct 30, residents acknowledged the added greenery but stressed it did not endorse the revised plans. Professor Hwang urges early collaboration for ecologically significant sites rather than treating opposition as grounds for reduced development.
items.title: NUS professor weighs revised Singapore forest housing plans

items.summary: Gidarjil Development Corporation has opened Nyamgim Gung, described as Australia's first Indigenous-led and regional water testing laboratory at the Bundaberg Port. Lab manager Nirali Vadgama said it enables faster analysis of samples collected by its rangers on country. CEO Margaret Blackman framed the lab as empowering traditional owners to manage sea country and build self-determination. The facility sits 400 kilometres north of Brisbane, was built since 2022, and holds national accreditation through the National Association of Testing Authorities.
items.title: Aboriginal-owned lab opens Australia's first Indigenous-led water testing facility

items.summary: Ellie Carpenter scored her fifth goal of the Women's Super League season, helping Chelsea defeat Charlton Athletic 6-0 at The Valley to stay top of the table. Chelsea remain level on points with reigning champions Manchester City after Mary Fowler assisted a late win over London City Lionesses. Tottenham Hotspur beat Birmingham City 4-1 to reach fourth, while Arsenal drew 1-1 against Aston Villa despite 28 attempts on goal.
items.title: Carpenter's fifth WSL goal as Chelsea beat Charlton 6-0

items.summary: Construction of a large over-the-horizon radar complex in Russia's Kaliningrad exclave is nearly complete, according to reports. Security expert Vaidotas Malinionis told DW the facility could see about 3,000 kilometers beyond the horizon and peer across Europe and Ukraine, though its operational readiness remains unconfirmed. The Times cites ICEYE on plans for electronic-signal detection and jamming. Analyst Evija Djatkovica warned it exposes NATO's eastern flank to surveillance while Russia readies nuclear options; she also noted the radar's size makes it an easy target. Germany is building SAR satellites with ICEYE, set to launch in early 2027, for use on NATO's eastern flank.
items.title: Kaliningrad's New Radar Draws NATO Alarm

items.summary: Rioters looted shops in central Frankfurt late on Saturday as clashes erupted across German cities over the cost of living, according to a BBC report. Thousands had joined largely peaceful demonstrations before violence broke out. At least 54 people were arrested and more than 100 police officers left injured, per German authorities. Outbreaks also occurred in Berlin, Cologne and Hamburg.
items.title: Protests in Germany turn violent amid cost-of-living anger

items.summary: David W. Ferguson, retired honorary chief English editor of Foreign Languages Press, argues in a CGTN opinion article that continuity is the fourth pillar underpinning China's political system, alongside cooperation, consultation and consensus. Writing anonymously on his own views, he contrasts China with the UK Labour Government's first autumn budget, which included a one-off 100 pounds cash payment to 20 million households. He links Party self-governance through anti-corruption campaigns and education programs to lessons from the Red Army's Long March, presenting integrity and education as vital to sustaining revolutionary ideals across generations amid global change. The article reflects the author's opinions and not necessarily CGTN's views.
items.title: Opinion piece frames continuity as a pillar of China's governance strength

items.summary: A CGTN commentary argues that Hong Kong's handling of the Wang Fuk Court fire in Tai Po District reflects its governance beyond emergency response. The blaze on November 26, 2025 claimed 168 lives and injured 79 people across seven buildings after roughly 43 hours of firefighting. An independent committee report released October 29, 2026 found serious shortcomings in construction and oversight while proposing safety reforms. The author frames the government's priorities as protecting life, supporting affected communities through resettlement and financial aid, and strengthening institutional safeguards, presenting accountability and compassion as complementary rather than competing.
items.title: Hong Kong frames humanitarian care as core of fire recovery

items.summary: Marta Shahbazi, a University of Cambridge researcher and group leader at the Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology, is named among at least 69 victims of a deadly train crash in Spain on Wednesday. She was travelling to collect the 2026 José Luis Gómez-Skarmeta prize when her train collided with a stationary Iryo service near Urda in Toledo.
items.title: Cambridge Scientist Among Spain Train Crash Victims

items.summary: The longest ceasefire in Ukraine's war ended Sunday after Russia declined an offer of extension, Ukrainian officials said. The truce had enabled a humanitarian mission to the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky and civilian evacuations as the conflict enters its fifth year. Residents called it 'a breath of fresh air', but a military officer warned fighting could resume worse than before amid reports that Russia moved troops during the pause.
items.title: Kherson Ceasefire Ends After Russia Rejects Extension

items.summary: Ignazio Cassis became the first Swiss foreign minister to visit North Korea since 2003, arriving on 29 and 30 October. Switzerland reopened its Pyongyang office on 19 October, which now falls under the embassy in Beijing after a 2020 closure during COVID-19. The trip aimed to restore political dialogue amid rising tensions as North Korea fired around 10 short-range ballistic missiles toward Thursday's sea.
items.title: Swiss Foreign Minister Reopens North Korea Office in First Visit Since 2003

items.summary: Crypto debit cards accessed through international providers like RedotPay have drawn attention from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), two persons told ET. Several Indian residents' access to pre-paid crypto cards has been blocked recently, and no confirmation was available from payment firms or the central bank. The non-profit Digital South Trust submitted findings on stablecoin-based offshore card programmes used for everyday payments in India. Legal experts say such arrangements may violate FEMA regulations because foreign custodian accounts convert cryptocurrency into fiat currency automatically.
items.title: RBI and FIU probe offshore crypto cards used in India

items.summary: Speaking at Kerala High Court's platinum jubilee, Chief Justice Surya Kant stressed the importance of timely court intervention and called for judicial introspection to improve case listing. He highlighted Article 226 as a key strength empowering high courts nationwide and questioned whether urgent matters can be identified more effectively through transparent procedures or technology. The CJI framed these questions as collective responsibility rather than criticism, noting SC respects HC autonomy over rosters.
items.title: Chief Justice of India urges judiciary introspection on responsiveness

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday that India recorded one of the world's fastest poverty declines, with extreme poverty collapsing by 90% between 2011 and 2023 to a low of 2. 6%. He cited World Bank figures stating nearly 50 crore people moved out of poverty over those years, employment grew by 13. 4 crore from 2017 to 2023, and the Gini index fell over 20% from 29 in 2011 to 23 in 2023. Modi called elimination of poverty a government commitment rather than slogan.
items.title: Modi Credits World Bank Data for India's Poverty Decline

items.summary: As tensions rise over possible US action against Iran, speculation grows that Americans could face a military draft if World War 3 breaks out. Although such a conflict would likely be fought in Gulf waters and by air, making conscription unlikely, the UK, Japan and France have urged citizens to assemble three-day emergency survival kits. A Mirror report notes mandatory service resembles the Vietnam-era lottery system; Foresight's Christopher Lee says only about 1.8 million men were drafted then (about 7% of population). The UK updated its reserves so Brits up to 65 could be called, and Lord Dannatt expects reservists mobilised first before conscription among 18-24-year-olds. Senator Chris Murphy warned the strategy risks devastating escalation. There is no indication the US plans to revive a draft lottery. (79 words)
items.title: US draft fears amid Iran war anxiety

items.summary: All nine people aboard a business jet were killed when it crashed into a South Florida neighbourhood on Sunday, US transportation secretary Sean Duffy said. The Learjet 60 departed from Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas before nose-diving into the area and bursting into flames. It appeared to narrowly miss nearby homes.
items.title: Nine Killed When Business Jet Crashes in South Florida

items.summary: The Winn family, heirs of artist James Buchanan Buck Winn Jr., has placed a permanent conservation easement on Four Winns Ranch near Wimberley in Hays County. Held by Hill Country Conservancy with the USDA's Natural Resources Conservation Service through its Agricultural Conservation Easement Program, the agreement protects 165 acres while allowing agriculture and ecotourism to continue. The property preserves wildlife habitat, historic stone fences dating around 1850, and water resources along Pierce Creek and the Blanco River, which contributes up to 6% of recharge reaching Barton Springs.
items.title: Winn Heirs Place Permanent Conservation Easement on Historic Texas Ranch

items.summary: Four members of NASA’s CHAPEA crew exited a simulated Mars mission after 378 days in isolation at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Medical officer Ellen Ellis and commander Ross Elder spoke about the year-long confinement, risks, patience, and lessons for future astronauts. The exercise supports NASA plans to return humans to the Moon before attempting missions to Mars as early as the 2030s.
items.title: NASA Crew Emerges After Nearly Four Months in Simulated Mars Mission

items.summary: Union Minister for Railways Ashwini Vaishnaw reviewed manufacturing of the Bharat-made B28 bullet train carbody at BEML's Aditya facility on Sunday, November 1, 2026. He inspected precision-engineered jigs and fixtures, production stages including underframe, sidewall and roof assembly, passenger seats, HVAC systems and couplers, plus a Squeeze Test quality demonstration. An official statement described the visit as an unattributed report of his review.
items.title: Railways Minister Reviews B28 Bullet Train Production at BEML Facility

items.summary: Wendy's faces falling sales and weaker customer traffic as it slips behind rivals in the US burger market, its share of industry sales dropping from 11.5% in 2019 to 10.4% in 2025. Billionaire investor Nelson Peltz's Trian Fund Management has made an unsolicited offer worth around $1.4 billion, valuing the company at $7.35 per share and representing a premium of nearly 19%. Wendy's confirmed on October 28 that it received the non-binding proposal, but its board formed an independent committee to review it. CEO Bob Wright acknowledged eroded quality differentiation in his own words.
items.title: Trian Offers $1.4 Billion to Take Wendy's Private Amid Sales Decline

items.summary: Yoav Segalovitz, a Jewish former police officer and self-described Zionist, is joining the conservative Arab-led Islamist party Ra’am after leaving a centrist Jewish-led party. According to an Associated Press report, he will enter the Knesset as part of an alliance with leader Mansour Abbas, who believes Jewish and Arab citizens can cooperate despite their differences. Segalovitz told AP before the election that although they differ in ethnicity and religion, all are Israeli citizens. The partnership faces criticism from right-wing critics accusing him of betrayal and left-wing Joint List members dismissing it as political branding. Ra’am won eight seats, while Arab-led parties collectively hold 19 of the Knesset's 120 seats, giving them potential influence in forming the next government.
items.title: Jewish Ex-Police Officer Joins Arab-Led Israeli Party Ra’am

items.summary: At the IISS Manama Dialogue in Bahrain, India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri said BRICS is not yet a defence cooperation platform. He noted that although the topic featured at recent summits, it has produced no concrete initiatives and remains "not really...a defence cooperation construct." Misri stressed prioritising diplomacy over conflict.
items.title: India's Foreign Secretary Says BRICS Lacks Defence Cooperation Framework

items.summary: The Bhopal Municipal Corporation plans to introduce around 150 electric vehicles for waste collection and road-cleaning after Diwali, its first major move toward an all-electric garbage fleet. It aims to convert the entire garbage-collection fleet by end of 2027, with annual savings estimated at Rs 3-4 crore. The corporation expects 120 new electric garbage vehicles by December, plus 20 road-sweeping machines (10 small and 10 large). BMC transport officer Vijay Goyal told Free Press the vehicles cover about 150 km per charge and run two to three days before recharging.
items.title: Bhopal Plans Electric Waste-Fleet Conversion With ₹4 Crore Savings Target

items.summary: The Hyderabad Cricket Association issued a press release listing the squad for the Fourth match of the ongoing BCCI Nayudu Trophy against Maharashtra. P. Aman Rao is named captain, Aaron George vice-captain, and A. Avanish Rao wicket-keeper. The roster includes G. Ritheesh Reddy, Wafi Kachchhi, A. Vignesh Reddy, Sunkara Dheeraj, Yash Sathwalekar, Pranav Varma, Ghazi Abbas, C. Advaith Reddy, Nishant Saranu, R. Dinesh Rathod, Harshit Sai Yelamanchili, and Tarun Rajan.
items.title: Hyderabad Names Under-23 Squad for Nayudu Trophy Clash with Maharashtra

items.summary: HPRC Artists beat HPRC Tigers 14-10 in the Arena Polo Tournament final at Hyderabad on Sunday evening, completing an unbeaten run. Arsalan Khan scored 2 goals late in the last chukker and finished with 4 in the first period, 3 in each of the next two, reaching a tournament total of 20 from three matches to win Most Valuable Player. Shehzad Alam Khan took the most promising young player award for scoring 8 across his debut.
items.title: Arsalan Khan Wins MVP Leading HPRC Artists To Polo Final Trophy

items.summary: Hemanth, an Andhra Pradesh man accused of attacking a Class 10 student with a chainsaw at her school in Anantapur district on Saturday morning, was injured in police firing while resisting arrest near Atmakur. Police fired six rounds after warning shots; the circle inspector who tried to protect the girl was also hurt. The victim remains critically injured and is being treated in Bengaluru.
items.title: Andhra cop assaulted with knife shot during arrest of chainsaw attacker

items.summary: Kishor Palve founded Bright Future in 2009 to help young people from underserved communities build self-reliance. He grew it from a small batch of students into an organisation reaching 26 communities, with 14 across Mumbai as its primary area. Its training centres offer personal and professional development over three-to-four months for youth aged 13 to 25.
items.title: Bright Future empowers Mumbai youth through mentorship and skills training

items.summary: The All Ladakh Liquor Traders Association questioned climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Saturday, challenging his call to make the Union Territory a dry region while drug use, smoking and meat consumption were not addressed. The association also raised questions about whether his home-grown apple wine brand 'Ule Topo' held the required government licence. Wangchuk had objected to the Excise Policy 2026-27 introduced on June 1, which proposed raising retail liquor outlets from two to 20. On October 28, the Ladakh administration rejected his claims as false and baseless, saying only one shop was operational under the restored policy while 50 outlets attached to restaurants operated across Ladakh.
items.title: Ladakh liquor traders challenge Wangchuk's dry-UT demand over licence and policy

items.summary: The Education Department of Haryana has suspended two Junior Basic Training (JBT) teachers, Simranjeet Kaur and Pooja Rani, with immediate effect over an alleged assault on a six-year-old girl at a government school in Panchkula. The family alleges the accused third-grade student led them to the injured child despite monitored CCTV cameras. The Haryana State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (HSCPCR) has taken suo motu cognisance and directed the District Education Officer, Panchkula, to submit a point-wise factual report on departmental action. Police registered an FIR under the Juvenile Justice Act and Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita against the school management for alleged negligence.
items.title: Two teachers suspended; child rights panel asks for report in Panchkula assault case

items.summary: The Indian government claims a booming formal job market, citing Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) payroll figures that reportedly more than doubled from 6.11 million in FY2018-19 to 13.15 million. The Economic Survey 2023–24 called this “healthy growth in formal employment,” and the Union Labour Ministry echoed it as a “growing formal employment landscape.” Skeptics argue an EPFO net subscriber addition is not necessarily a new job, since it can reflect movement between employers or administrative changes. Supporting evidence from NSS/ASI data shows organised manufacturing added 5.7 million jobs (FY2015–FY2024), but contract labour share rose to 40.7% by 2022-23, and PLFS data show informal workers still at about 90%, with youth unemployment doubling from 6% in 2012 to 12% in 2024.
items.title: India's formal-jobs claim faces scrutiny over EPFO data
